lesson_title: Rural Settlements: Where, How and Why
hook_text: A village's shape is never an accident. Roads, water and cattle drew it.
clip_script: Picture a handful of dried mealie kernels. Fling them across the floor and they land far apart, each alone — that is dispersed settlement, one homestead here, the next one kilometres away, exactly what commercial farm country looks like. Now instead drop all the kernels into one pot — that is nucleated settlement, homes packed together in a cluster with the fields lying around the outside. Scattered kernels, private land; one pot, shared land. That single link — pattern to land ownership — is the reason-mark the exam is fishing for.
visual_style: Overhead shot of mealie kernels scattering then pooling in a pot, dissolving into aerial views of Free State farmsteads and a nucleated Eastern Cape village.
pacing: Quick tactile hook, one clean contrast, confident landing.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read any village off the map — pattern, shape and function.
